input.strategy_title: AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for serving and training
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Two strategic customers are standardizing on AMD Instinct accelerators and need
RHOAI to serve and train on ROCm. Upstream vLLM and PyTorch both publish ROCm
support, but the platform ships only CUDA runtime builds, and we have no
first-hand data on functional or performance parity for our supported model
set. Feature and performance validation requires physical AMD GPU hardware —
none exists in our CI fleet today — and upstream ROCm image cadence is
controlled by AMD and the upstream communities.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Serving Runtimes
- Training Operator
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- Intel Gaudi or other non-AMD accelerator families
- AMD GPU sharing/partitioning support

## Open Questions

1. Hardware access: the validation campaign (HLR-1) needs dedicated AMD
   Instinct nodes — procurement or partner-lab access is unresolved.
2. Upstream ROCm build cadence: whether AMD's runtime image releases align
   with our release trains is outside our control.

# AMD Instinct validation campaign: vLLM ROCm serving functional and performance parity

## Description

This epic runs the validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct accelerators that establishes first-hand functional and performance parity data for vLLM ROCm serving of the supported model set, and produces the go/no-go scope that determines which models are productized. It resolves the strategy's central unknown — whether upstream vLLM ROCm builds deliver acceptable parity for our supported models — which the serving runtime productization work is gated on.

## Scope

- Secure access to dedicated AMD Instinct GPU nodes (via procurement or partner-lab access); the access grant itself is externally controlled and tracked as a risk, while the epic's deliverable is the validated parity report.
- Stand up vLLM ROCm serving on the AMD Instinct nodes using upstream ROCm runtime builds, deployed through the platform serving stack (InferenceServices served by a vLLM ROCm runtime), so parity is measured on the path users will actually run.
- For every model in the supported model set, run functional validation of vLLM serving on ROCm and record pass/fail against defined correctness criteria.
- For every model in the supported model set, measure serving performance (throughput and latency) on AMD Instinct hardware and record a comparison against the CUDA baseline.
- Compile the campaign report: per-model functional and performance results, environment details (driver, ROCm, runtime image versions), and the explicit go/no-go scope — the list of models cleared for productization.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A functional parity result (pass/fail against defined criteria) is recorded for every model in the supported model set.
- Performance measurements (throughput and latency) are recorded for every model in the supported model set on AMD Instinct hardware, alongside a CUDA baseline comparison.
- The serving path is exercised through the platform serving stack: InferenceServices deployed via KServe using a vLLM ROCm runtime on AMD GPU nodes, confirming the serving control plane requires no code changes for AMD accelerators.
- The final report states the go/no-go scope: the explicit list of models cleared for productization, with the supporting evidence.
- All results are reproducible from the recorded job configurations and environment versions (driver, ROCm, runtime image digests).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization.

## Risks / Notes

- Hardware access is unresolved (procurement or partner-lab); the grant timing is externally controlled and is the strategy's highest schedule risk. The acceptance criteria sit on the epic's deliverable (the validated report), not on the availability of hardware.

# Productize supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for campaign-cleared models

## Description

This epic productizes a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the models the validation campaign clears: a midstream ROCm image build of the vLLM runtime, its productized serving runtime definition, and release through the existing build pipeline — turning the validated upstream capability into a supported platform runtime.

## Scope

- Build and release the vLLM ROCm runtime image variant from the midstream vLLM repository, based on a published upstream ROCm release pinned for the platform release train.
- Add the ROCm serving runtime definition (ServingRuntime) for AMD GPU nodes to the productized runtime set, scoped to the models cleared by the validation campaign.
- Extend the existing build pipeline configuration in the already-onboarded midstream repository to build the ROCm image variant.
- Verify integration with the serving stack: InferenceServices using the ROCm runtime deploy and serve on AMD GPU nodes through KServe with no serving control-plane code changes.
- Record the supported-model scope, hardware, and driver prerequisites that the runtime is supported for.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ROCm vLLM runtime image builds green in the existing build pipeline for the midstream repository.
- A productized ServingRuntime using the ROCm image deploys InferenceServices that serve every model on the campaign's cleared list on AMD GPU nodes.
- The runtime's supported-model scope exactly matches the go/no-go list produced by the validation campaign.
- The shipped runtime pins a published upstream ROCm release, and the pinned version is recorded.
- The rollout is additive and reversible: existing CUDA runtimes are unaffected, and the ROCm runtime can be disabled or removed without impacting them.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears.

## Risks / Notes

- Upstream ROCm runtime image cadence is controlled by AMD and the upstream communities; alignment with platform release trains is an externally controlled schedule risk. Mitigated by pinning to a published upstream ROCm release (acceptance criterion above) rather than tracking a moving tag.
- This epic is gated on the validation campaign's go/no-go outcome; its scope is rewritten to the cleared model list, and it is removed entirely if no models clear.

# PyTorch ROCm training support for single- and multi-GPU PyTorchJobs

## Description

This epic makes PyTorch training on ROCm supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs run through the Training Operator: PyTorchJob workers schedule onto AMD Instinct GPU nodes, run with upstream PyTorch ROCm images, and are admitted through Kueue with amd.com/gpu quota and gang semantics.

## Scope

- Enable PyTorchJob worker pods to schedule onto AMD GPU nodes with `amd.com/gpu` resources (node labels/affinity and tolerations as needed for AMD-accelerated nodes).
- Validate single-GPU PyTorchJob execution on ROCm using upstream PyTorch ROCm images.
- Validate multi-GPU / multi-worker PyTorchJob execution on ROCm across AMD Instinct GPUs, with jobs admitted through Kueue queueing.
- Capture any Training Operator changes or configuration required for ROCm execution, and record the validated driver, ROCm, and image versions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob runs to completion on an AMD Instinct GPU node requesting `amd.com/gpu` resources.
- A multi-GPU, multi-worker PyTorchJob runs to completion across AMD Instinct GPUs.
- Jobs are admitted through Kueue queueing with `amd.com/gpu` quota accounted correctly (requires the Kueue AMD GPU quota handling capability).
- Validation is performed on AMD Instinct hardware with the driver, ROCm, and image versions recorded for reproducibility.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)**: PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling.

## Risks / Notes

- Validation requires access to the AMD Instinct hardware pool shared with the serving validation campaign — a coordination risk, not a dependency.

# Kueue amd.com/gpu quota handling for training workload admission

## Description

This epic delivers Kueue admission and quota handling for AMD GPUs so that training workloads requesting `amd.com/gpu` resources are admitted with correct quota accounting and all-or-nothing gang semantics — the queueing foundation that PyTorch ROCm training jobs are admitted through.

## Scope

- Extend the Distributed Workloads quota model to cover `amd.com/gpu` resources (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue resource flavors for AMD GPU nodes).
- Ensure workloads requesting `amd.com/gpu` are admitted with the platform's all-or-nothing semantics so multi-GPU training jobs are not partially admitted.
- Validate quota accounting, queueing, and admission of `amd.com/gpu`-requesting workloads on a cluster with AMD GPU nodes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A workload requesting `amd.com/gpu` is admitted only when quota is available and stays pending when it is not (quota accounting is correct for the AMD GPU resource).
- Multi-pod workloads requesting `amd.com/gpu` are admitted all-or-nothing (gang semantics hold for AMD GPU jobs).
- Quota configuration and admission behavior are validated on AMD GPU nodes with the validated setup recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)**: PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling.

## Risks / Notes

- Validation benefits from access to the AMD Instinct hardware pool shared with the serving validation campaign — a coordination risk, not a dependency.

# AMD ROCm support documentation (hardware, drivers, validated models)

## Description

This epic authors the user-facing documentation for AMD GPU (ROCm) support: the supported AMD hardware, the driver prerequisites, and the validated model list, covering both serving with the ROCm vLLM runtime and PyTorch training admitted through Kueue.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Supported AMD hardware: the AMD Instinct accelerators supported for serving and training.
- Driver prerequisites: the AMD driver and ROCm versions required on worker nodes.
- Validated model list: the models cleared by the validation campaign, matching the productized runtime's supported scope.
- Serving usage: deploying InferenceServices with the vLLM ROCm serving runtime on AMD GPU nodes.
- Training usage: running single- and multi-GPU PyTorchJobs on AMD GPUs, admitted through Kueue with `amd.com/gpu` quota.
- Limitations: AMD GPU sharing/partitioning is not supported (out of scope for the strategy).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation topics state the supported AMD hardware, the driver prerequisites, and the validated model list.
- The documented model list matches the go/no-go list produced by the validation campaign and the productized runtime's supported scope.
- Serving and training usage topics describe the shipped capabilities accurately (runtime deployment and Kueue-admitted training as implemented).
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior by both owning teams (serving and distributed workloads).
- Technical claims are validated against the platform architecture context for the affected components.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)**: Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list.

graph TD

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 3 (Investigation gates downstream) | The campaign's go/no-go outcome determines which models the productized runtime supports — a true gate (`rewrite`: scope narrows to cleared models; if no model clears, productization is removed). |
| E004 → E003 | Rule 12 (framework → consumer) | PyTorchJob training admission through Kueue with amd.com/gpu quota builds on the quota/admission capability; multi-GPU gang admission cannot be validated before quota handling exists. |

| E004 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Docs describe amd.com/gpu quota usage. |

No edge between E001/E002 and E003/E004: serving and training streams are architecturally distinct (different components, different teams, no shared artifact). They share only the AMD hardware pool — a coordination risk recorded in Health Warnings, not a dependency. No `konflux-onboarding` epic is generated (see Component Mapping Notes).

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) | Notes |
|-----|----------|---------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | E001 | Validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware; produces go/no-go scope. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | E002 | Productization of the vLLM ROCm serving runtime, scoped to cleared models. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | E003, E004 | Split along component boundary (Training Operator vs. Distributed Workloads), both owned by the Distributed Workloads team. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | E005 | Docs epic priority is P1 via the docs-authoring priority exception (strategy priority `Major` → P1), not P2. |

All four HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements. No redundant/overlapping HLR pairs were found, and no lower-priority HLR is bundled into a higher-priority epic (HLR-3's two-epic split is a component boundary split, not a priority split).

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections**: the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and no Non-Functional Requirements section. Epic acceptance criteria were derived from the HLR text; owner teams were inferred from `.context/architecture-context/` owning-team fields (RHOAI Serving for KServe/Serving Runtimes; Distributed Workloads for Training Operator/Distributed Workloads). Human verification of team assignments recommended.
- **Hardware availability (Open Question 1)** is an availability precondition externally controlled (procurement or partner-lab access), not a DAG node or acceptance criterion. The validation campaign epic includes *securing* access as part of its work, and its acceptance criteria sit on the deliverable (the validated parity report). If access stalls, the entire strategy slips — highest-schedule-risk item.
- **Upstream ROCm image cadence (Open Question 2)** is externally controlled timing. It does not change which epics exist, so it is recorded as a schedule risk on the runtime productization epic (with a pinned-upstream-release acceptance criterion), not as an Investigation or an edge.
- **KServe treated as passive**: KServe is listed as an affected component but no code changes are anticipated — InferenceService deployment on AMD GPU nodes is exercised as acceptance criteria on the campaign and productization epics. If campaign findings reveal KServe changes are needed, a KServe epic must be added.
- **E001 size watch item (re-split trigger)**: the validation campaign is one logical pass over the full supported model set on externally scheduled hardware and could exceed the ~2-week epic guideline. It is intentionally not split — a split would duplicate the campaign (shared hardware access, per-model job configurations, and a single parity report) and fragment the go/no-go deliverable that E002's scope depends on. Re-split trigger: if the campaign outgrows a sprint of effort, split it along model-family lines, or split performance benchmarking out of functional validation.
- **Documentation epic team**: the docs epic spans both teams' output (serving + training); it is assigned to RHOAI Serving (owner of the P0 stream) and must be technically reviewed by both teams.

## Component Mapping Notes

- All epic `component` values are copied verbatim from `.context/rhai-components.txt`: `Serving Runtimes` (E001, E002), `Training Operator` (E003), `Distributed Workloads` (E004), `Documentation` (E005).
- **KServe**: passive — validated as acceptance criteria on E001/E002 (see Health Warnings).
- **No `konflux-onboarding` epic**: the midstream vLLM repo is already Konflux-onboarded per `.context/architecture-context/architecture/rhoai-3.0/serving-runtimes.md`.
